result:
The api went down because the disk filled up: the `report-export` job wrote about 20 GB of CSVs into `/var/lib/stockroom/exports`, Postgres ran out of space on the same volume, and the api exited at 03:14:06 and never came back.

One thing to check first: every timestamp in `logs/service.log` is 2026-03-09 (02:00–05:30), not last night. Either this is an old log or the clock/filename is off, so confirm it's the incident you mean.

## Timeline

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 02:00–03:05 | Normal traffic, all requests returning 200. |
| 03:05:00 | `report-export` starts writing 512 MB CSV parts to `/var/lib/stockroom/exports`, one every 12 seconds. |
| 03:09:03 | `WARN disk /var/lib/stockroom at 91%` |
| 03:12:48 | Last export part written (40 parts, about 20 GB in under 8 minutes). |
| 03:13:30 | `WARN disk /var/lib/stockroom at 99%` |
| 03:14:00 | `ERROR db: could not extend file "base/16384/2619": No space left on device` |
| 03:14:03 | `ERROR api: transaction aborted, shutting down worker pool` |
| 03:14:06 | `FATAL api: exiting (status 1)` |
| 03:16:00–05:28:00 | `ERROR proxy: upstream api refused connection` every 2 minutes until the log ends. |

## What the log shows beyond the crash

- **No recovery:** there is not a single api request after 03:14, and the proxy was still being refused at 05:28, so the outage ran at least 2h15m. The log has no restart attempts or api startup lines, even though `docker-compose.yml` sets `restart: unless-stopped` on the api.
- **Partial outage:** `web` and `proxy` kept serving 200s the whole time; only the api-backed path was down.
- **Unrelated noise:** the `cache: slow command` warnings (100–150 ms, roughly every 5 minutes) run from 02:00 through the end at the same rate, so they are not part of this.

## What the log doesn't show

- Why the export produced that much data, or what triggered it at 03:05. Nothing in `app/` or `scripts/` references `report-export`, so the job is defined somewhere outside this repo.
- Whether the export stopped on its own or died when the disk filled.
- Whether the space has since been freed. If those CSVs are still there, the api will fail again as soon as it is started.

The underlying problem is that the exports and the database share one volume with no cap on the export job, and the 91% warning five minutes before the crash did not prompt any action.
